title: The Bleak Truth Behind France’s Riots
author: Michael C. Behrent
content:
![The Bleak Truth Behind France’s
Riots](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/10/AP26273323627439.jpg)

Hegel said that a tragic situation is one in which both sides are right. The
violence that has recently broken out at French high schools comfortably fits
this definition. On the one hand, a movement supported by leftists--notably
Jean-Luc Melenchon's party, _La France insoumise_ (Unbowed France) or LFI--is
protesting against inadequate resources and the dire state of many _lyc ees
_(high schools). On the other side are the French state and its security
forces, which are responding forcefully to the protesters' brazen rejection of
elementary standards of civic behavior. The violence in which the movement has
engaged is indeed deplorable, resulting in the destruction of several schools
and the beating of police officers. At the same time, the French government's
police state reflexes are also on full display. Yet this exclusive focus on
violence overlooks the fact that, despite all that sets them against each
other, the grievances expressed by parties in the conflict are surprisingly
similar.

> "France manages to combine the worst elements of neoliberalism with the
> worst elements of social democracy."

Even as they fight one another, the students and the police have both
experienced the profound degradation of French public services in recent
years. Both represent institutions that feel they no longer have the means to
carry out the tasks they are expected to fulfill. Both, moreover, have
suffered from the policies France has pursued for decades, and which have been
heightened during President Emmanuel Macron's decade in power. The French
state has increasingly adopted neoliberal approaches to public management,
even as it borrowed money at astronomical rates. France manages to combine the
worst elements of neoliberalism with the worst elements of social democracy.
Financial incoherence is matched by political dysfunction. For all intents and
purposes, France lacks and seems incapable of finding a governing majority.
Many fear that the chaos afflicting many high schools is merely a foretaste of
the civil discord that could erupt during next year's presidential election.
